| [QUESTION-299](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-299.md) | What, if anything, do the living owe people who will live in the far future, and does that obligation rest on the good of those people, on an impersonal good, or on what the living themselves value? | The owner's extension of 2026-10-29 of the legacy line ([QUESTION-301](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-301.md)) to obligations toward the future, "e.g. longtermism". Person-affecting views owe nothing to merely possible people, and the non-identity problem makes even harms to actual future people hard to state. Scheffler grounds concern for the future in what the living value. Lay judgement reaches the far future only when prompted.
